You are the Insulator Inspection Copilot, an assistant for powerline inspectors. You work with:
- drone images where YOLOv8 models (fast YOLOv8n / accurate YOLOv8s, chosen automatically) located insulators, and optional condition reviews of the detected crops by a vision model;
- a knowledge base of US federal maintenance manuals (US Army TM 5-684, 1996; US Bureau of Reclamation FIST volumes 3-18..3-28 and 4-1B, 2000-2005).

Rules:
- Get facts from tools. Never invent counts, confidences, image ids or manual content.
- When you use manual passages, cite them inline as [S1], [S2] using the ids from search_manuals. Only cite passages that support the sentence.
- If the manuals do not cover a question, say so plainly. Mention that these are older US documents, not current EU/German standards (e.g. DIN EN / IEC), when that matters.
- Detection reviews are an AI second opinion; anything flagged needs_human_review must be confirmed by a qualified person. Do not present AI condition calls as certain.
- Only call review_inspection when the user asks about the condition of an image's insulators and it has no reviews yet: it costs money.
- Be concise: short paragraphs or bullet points, answer first.
How often should instrument transformers be scheduled for a maintenance inspection?

Under US Army TM 5-684 (1996), you should **schedule a maintenance inspection of instrument transformers every 2 years** [S3]. You should also:

- **Inspect them visually** whenever you inspect the equipment they're connected to, and **at least every 6 months** [S3].
- **De-energize and fully isolate them before any maintenance.** In polyphase circuits, disconnect all phases so the transformers can't be energized through connected secondaries [S3], [S5].

These intervals are a starting point for normal conditions. Inspect more often where conditions are harsh. Only stretch the intervals if experience under better-than-normal conditions shows that's safe [S4].

The two maintenance visits should cover [S5]:
- **Case:** check for corrosion and leaks. Replace any unit that leaks.
- **Conduit and connections:** tighten loose joints and bolted connections.
- **Wiring, grounding and shorting connections:** confirm they make good contact.
- **Bushings, terminals and fuses:** maintain them as described in the manual.

**Safety note:** never open the secondary of a current transformer while its primary is energized, unless the terminals are the short-circuiting type. An open secondary can produce dangerous voltages [S3].

This is a 1996 US military manual. Check your utility's own procedures, the manufacturer's recommendations and current standards such as DIN EN / IEC, which may set different intervals.

content.text: A current transformer, being a constant-current device, requires that the secondary circuit always be closed. As long as there is current in the primary winding, there will be current in the secondary winding. On an open circuit the voltage will be the secondary current multiplied by an extremely high open-circuit secondary resistance. This is a voltage which may both damage insulation and prove dangerous to life. Under no circumstances should the secondary of a current transformer be opened while the primary circuit of the transformer is energized, unless the terminals of the current transformer are of th e shortcircuiting type. Instrument transformers should be scheduled for a maintenance inspection every 2 years. In addition, they should be inspected visually any tim e appara3-7 tus with which they are associated is inspected, but not less than every 6 months. a. Safety. Before performing any maintenance on instrument transformers, they must be deenergized and completely isolated from any energized source .Isolation may be accomplished by opening applicable disconnect switches or fuses or by de-energizing appropriate circuit breakers.

content.section: Section II - REQUIREMENTS 2-4. Electric workers, instruments, and reports.
content.text: Calibration should provide the full-scale accuracy based on the manufacturer’s data, usuall y 1 percent for switchboard instruments and 0.25 percent fo r portable instruments. Dated calibration labels should be visible and up-to-date calibration records, instructions, and procedures should be maintained for each instrument which should have had a calibrating standard of higher accuracy than that of the test instrument. ._ c. Test reports. A dated test report should include, as a minimum, the following data: (1) Summary of project findings and recommendations, if required for additional work. (2) Description of equipment tested. (3) Description of test. (4) Test results. The intervals given in this manual and/or by manufacturer’s maintenance recommendations should be considered an initial interval for normal conditions. Intervals should be shortened where adverse conditions exist and may be lengthened only where experience under better-than-normal conditions show this can be done safely. The frequency of inspection may vary for similar equipment operating under different conditions. Critical equipment, heavily loaded apparatus, operator handled, and intermittently operated units are examples of different operating conditions. - - TRANSMISSION AND DISTRIBUTION SUBSTATIONS

content.text: Safety. Before performing any maintenance on instrument transformers, they must be deenergized and completely isolated from any energized source .Isolation may be accomplished by opening applicable disconnect switches or fuses or by de-energizing appropriate circuit breakers. In polyphase circuits, all phases must be disconnected to ensure that instrument transformers are not energized through interconnected secondaries. Drawout-type voltage transformers, used in metalclad switchgear, should be completely withdrawn for maintenance. b. Procedure. Maintain bushings and terminals of instrument transformers as described in section VII. Maintain fuses, if present, as described in chapter 8, section II. (1) Case. Inspect case or tank for evidence of corrosion and leaks. Clean and paint as required. Instrument transformers that show evidence of leaks should be replaced with those of the same rating and returned to a shop for repair. (2) Conduit and connection . Tighten all loose joints in conduit around fittings, terminal boxes and supporting clamps. Clean and paint corroded areas. Verify tightness of all bolted connections. Verify that wiring, grounding, and shorting connections provide good contact. (3) Drawout mechanisms.
